metric_rationale: The experimental design contrasts TTB and WADD using compensatory trials. On trials where the total number of positive features differs between options A and B, TTB always favors the option with the single most valid cue, which by design has *fewer* total positive features. Conversely, WADD integrates all cues, and the sum of the less valid cues outweighs the single most valid cue, meaning WADD systematically chooses the option with *more* positive features. This metric calculates the proportion of these conflict trials where the subject chooses the option with fewer positive features. TTB will score near 1.0, while WADD will score near 0.0.

The experimental design pits the single best discriminating cue (which dictates the Take The Best choice) against a coalition of multiple lower-validity cues (which favor the Weighted Additive choice). This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice aligns with the prediction of the Take The Best heuristic. Under TTB, this proportion will be very high (close to 1, modulo noise), whereas under WADD, the compensatory nature of the trials will drive choices toward the opposite option, yielding a significantly lower proportion.

This metric isolates the 'conflict' trials where Tallying and WADD make opposite predictions. Specifically, it identifies trials where one option has more positive features (favored by Tallying) but a lower validity-weighted sum (disfavored by WADD). The metric calculates the proportion of choices on these conflict trials that align with Tallying's prediction. Tallying will produce a high value (close to 1), whereas WADD will produce a low value (close to 0), maximizing the discrimination between the two theories.

This metric isolates the critical dissociation trials where WADD and Tallying make strictly opposite predictions. In these trials, one option has two high-validity features ([1, 1, 0, 0, 0]) and the other has three low-validity features ([0, 0, 1, 1, 1]). Tallying simply counts features and prefers the option with three features. WADD weights by validity and strongly prefers the option with two high-validity features. By computing the proportion of choices that favor the two-feature option, we expect a value > 0.5 for WADD and < 0.5 for Tallying, yielding a massive and highly reliable gap.
